name: Bela-Bela
meaning: Setswana for ‘the pot that boils’ – after the hot springs the town was built around.
formerNameOrigin: Warmbad (Warmbaths in English) meant the same thing: ‘warm bath’.

name: Bhisho
meaning: Usually explained as the isiXhosa word for buffalo, which is also the name of the river here. The new spelling is the standard isiXhosa one.

name: Cacadu
meaning: ‘Bulrush water’ – the isiXhosa name for the White Kei River, which rises in the district.
formerNameOrigin: Lady Frere was named after the wife of Sir Henry Bartle Frere, Cape governor from 1877 to 1880.

name: Cape Town International Airport
formerNameOrigin: Named after D. F. Malan, prime minister when the airport opened in 1954.

name: Centane
meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

name: Centurion
formerNameOrigin: Verwoerdburg (1967) was named after prime minister Hendrik Verwoerd, regarded as the architect of apartheid.

name: Dikeni
formerNameOrigin: Alice was named in 1847 after Princess Alice, Queen Victoria's second daughter.

name: Dutywa
meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

name: eMakhazeni
formerNameOrigin: Belfast was named after the Northern Irish birthplace of Richard Charles O'Neil, who owned the farm.

name: Emalahleni
meaning: ‘Place of coal’.
formerNameOrigin: Witbank is Afrikaans for ‘white ridge’, after a white sandstone outcrop.

name: eManzana
meaning: ‘Healing waters’ – the name Swazi people gave the hot spring here.
formerNameOrigin: Badplaas is Afrikaans for ‘bath farm’.

name: eManzimtoti
meaning: ‘Sweet water’ – said to be King Shaka's words on tasting the river. He used ‘mtoti’ instead of the usual ‘mnandi’ out of respect for his mother, Nandi.

name: eMaxesibeni
formerNameOrigin: Mount Ayliff was possibly named after William Ayliff, a Cape official, or John Ayliff, a mission founder.

name: eMdloti
meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiZulu spelling; the e- at the start means ‘at’ or ‘the place of’.

name: Emgwenya
formerNameOrigin: Waterval Boven is Dutch for ‘above the waterfall’.

name: eMkhomazi
meaning: ‘Place of the cow whales’ – whales were seen in the river mouth.

name: eMkhondo
formerNameOrigin: Piet Retief was named after the Voortrekker leader Piet Retief.

name: eMkhuze
meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiZulu spelling; the e- at the start means ‘at’ or ‘the place of’.

name: eMthunzini
meaning: ‘A place in the shade’ in isiZulu.

name: eNtokozweni
meaning: ‘Place of happiness’.
formerNameOrigin: Machadodorp honoured Portuguese Major Joachim Machado (1894).

name: eXobho
meaning: An isiZulu word imitating the squelch of cattle walking through mud.

name: Gariep Dam
meaning: Gariep is Khoekhoe for ‘river’ – the original name of the Orange River, which the dam holds back.
formerNameOrigin: Originally named after prime minister Hendrik Verwoerd.

name: Gcuwa
formerNameOrigin: Butterworth was named after Joseph Butterworth.

name: Gqeberha
meaning: The isiXhosa and Southern Khoe name for the Baakens River, which runs through the city. It is also the isiXhosa name for Walmer Township, one of the city's oldest townships.
formerNameOrigin: Port Elizabeth was named in 1820 by acting governor Sir Rufane Donkin after his late wife, Elizabeth.

name: James Calata
meaning: Honours Canon James Arthur Calata (1895–1983), Anglican priest in nearby Cradock for forty years and ANC secretary-general from 1936 to 1949.
formerNameOrigin: Jamestown was named after James Wagenaar, who owned the farm the town was laid out on.

name: Kariega
meaning: The area's original inhabitants called the Swartkops River the Kariega River, and the wider region from Willowmore and Somerset East to Uitenhage was once called Kariega.

name: Khowa
formerNameOrigin: Elliot was named after Sir Henry George Elliot, chief magistrate of the Transkeian territories from 1891 to 1902.

name: King Phalo Airport
formerNameOrigin: Named after Ben Schoeman, the minister of transport at the time.

name: Komani
formerNameOrigin: Queenstown was named after Queen Victoria.

name: KuGompo City
meaning: From Gompo Rock (Cove Rock) on the coast, a sacred place for amaXhosa. The name is said to echo the waves breaking on it – ‘gompo, gompo’. ‘City’ was added because a small town already had the name KuGompo.

name: KwaBhaca
meaning: ‘Place of the Bhaca people’ – the village of the amaBhaca chiefdom.
formerNameOrigin: Mount Frere was named after Sir Henry Bartle Frere.

name: KwaDukuza
meaning: ‘Place of the lost person’ in isiZulu – after the maze of huts at King Shaka's royal capital here.
formerNameOrigin: Stanger (1873) was named after William Stanger, surveyor-general of Natal.

name: KwaGingindlovu
meaning: ‘Swallower of the elephant’ – one of Cetshwayo's military homesteads, named for his 1856 victory over his brother Mbuyazi.

name: KwaMaqoma
meaning: Honours Maqoma, the Xhosa warrior chief who resisted British colonial forces in this area.
formerNameOrigin: Fort Beaufort was named after the Duke of Beaufort.

name: KwaNojoli
meaning: Honours Nojoli, a royal figure in the history of the amaXhosa of this area.

name: Lephalale
meaning: Named after the main river here; from a Setswana word meaning ‘to flow’.
formerNameOrigin: Ellisras combined the surnames of settlers Patrick Ellis and Piet Erasmus.

name: Mahikeng
meaning: ‘Place among rocks’ in Setswana. British settlers wrote it as Mafeking.

name: Makhanda
meaning: Honours Makhanda ka Nxele, the Xhosa warrior and prophet who led the 1819 attack on the British garrison here and was later imprisoned on Robben Island.
formerNameOrigin: Grahamstown was named after Colonel John Graham, who oversaw its founding in 1812.

name: Malalane
meaning: Same name, with a corrected spelling.

name: Maletswai
formerNameOrigin: Aliwal North was named by Sir Harry Smith after his victory over the Sikhs at the Battle of Aliwal.

name: Maloti
meaning: Same name, now written with the Sesotho spelling (Maloti rather than Maluti).

name: Mashishing
meaning: ‘Long green grass’ in Sepedi – what the Bapedi called the area.
formerNameOrigin: Lydenburg comes from the Dutch Lijdenburg, ‘town of suffering’.

name: Mbizana
meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

name: Mbombela
meaning: ‘Many people together in a small space’ in siSwati.
formerNameOrigin: Nelspruit was named after the Nel family who grazed cattle here, with spruit, an Afrikaans word for a stream.

name: Modimolle
meaning: From the Sotho-Tswana Modimo o lle, ‘the spirit has eaten’ or ‘God has eaten’ – the local name of a hill here.
formerNameOrigin: Nylstroom: the Voortrekkers thought the river was the Nile (Nyl) and the hill a pyramid.

name: Modjadjiskloof
meaning: Honours Rain Queen Modjadji, hereditary ruler of the Lobedu people. It keeps the Afrikaans -kloof (ravine).
formerNameOrigin: Duiwelskloof is Afrikaans for ‘Devil's ravine’.

name: Mokopane
meaning: Honours King (Chief) Mokopane, also written Makapan, of the Kekana Ndebele.
formerNameOrigin: Potgietersrus remembered Voortrekker leader Piet Potgieter, killed in 1854 during the Siege of Makapansgat.

name: Mookgophong
formerNameOrigin: Naboomspruit means ‘euphorbia tree stream’, after the Euphorbia ingens (naboom) trees.

name: Mthatha
meaning: Named after the Mthatha River, which takes its name from the sneezewood (umthathi) trees along it, known for their wood and medicinal uses.

name: Musina
meaning: TshiVenda for copper, from a root meaning ‘spoil’ – copper ‘spoilt’ early efforts to mine gold here.

name: Ngcobo
meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

name: Ngqamakhwe
meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

name: Ngqeleni
meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

name: Nqanqarhu
meaning: The town began in 1876 as a military camp called Nqanqaru Drift.
formerNameOrigin: Maclear was named after astronomer Sir Thomas Maclear.

name: Ntabankulu
meaning: Same name, now written in standard isiXhosa spelling.

name: Ntabozuko
formerNameOrigin: Berlin was founded in 1857 by German settlers and named after the German capital.

name: Nxuba
formerNameOrigin: Cradock was named after Sir John Cradock, governor of the Cape Colony in the early 1800s.

name: O. R. Tambo International Airport
meaning: Honours Oliver Reginald Tambo (1917–1993), anti-apartheid leader and president of the ANC from 1967 to 1991.
formerNameOrigin: Opened in 1952 as Jan Smuts International Airport, after the former prime minister.

name: oThongathi
meaning: From the uThongathi River. In isiZulu it means ‘it is important to us’ or ‘you are important because of us’, linked to legends about King Shaka.

name: Polokwane
meaning: ‘Sanctuary’ in Sepedi (Northern Sotho) – a name Sepedi speakers already used for the area.
formerNameOrigin: Pietersburg (1886) honoured Voortrekker leader Petrus Jacobus (Piet) Joubert.

name: Qonce
meaning: The Khoikhoi name for the Buffalo River, on which the town stands.
formerNameOrigin: King William's Town was named after King William IV.

name: Robert Sobukwe Town
meaning: Honours Robert Mangaliso Sobukwe, who was born here, anti-apartheid leader and founding president of the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC).
formerNameOrigin: Graaff-Reinet was named after Cape governor Cornelis Jacob van de Graaff and his wife.

name: uMnambithi
formerNameOrigin: Ladysmith (1850) was named after Juana María de los Dolores de León Smith, wife of governor Sir Harry Smith.

name: Mamafubedu
formerNameOrigin: The town was to be called Concordia, but Petrus Paulus Steyn's widow sold the land on condition that it was named after her late husband.

name: Hlohlolwane
meaning: From Sesotho words meaning 'get up and fight', after a dispute between the Bakwena and Baphuthi over a maize harvest.
formerNameOrigin: Clocolan is how newer residents said 'Hlohlolwane'.

name: Winnie Mandela
meaning: Honours Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, who was banished to the town in 1977. Her house there is now a museum.
formerNameOrigin: Brandfort was named after Johannes Brand, President of the Orange Free State, who visited soon after the town was founded in 1874.

name: Tlokoeng
meaning: Sesotho for 'place of the Tlokoa clan'.
formerNameOrigin: Mount Fletcher was named after the nearby mountain, probably after Reverend John Fletcher, a friend of John Wesley.

name: Gxarha
formerNameOrigin: Morgan's Bay was named in 1822 after A. F. Morgan, master of the survey ship Barracouta.

name: Solomon Linda
meaning: Honours Solomon Linda, the musician born here, a pioneer of isicathamiya choral music.
formerNameOrigin: Pomeroy was named after Sir George Pomeroy Colley, the British commander at the Battle of Majuba Hill in 1881.

name: Bishop Limba
formerNameOrigin: Adendorp was named after N. J. Adendorff, who owned the farm and divided it into smallholdings around 1858.

name: eMthonjaneni
formerNameOrigin: Melmoth was named after Sir Melmoth Osborn, the British resident commissioner of Zululand.

name: Ntshingwayo Dam
meaning: Honours Inkosi Ntshingwayo kaMahole Khoza, a senior general in King Cetshwayo's army who commanded at the Battle of Isandlwana in 1879.
